criteria.criterion: AC1: `rebar review <id>` runs the plan-review gate and returns its exit code; verified by test_review_forwards_to_review_plan
AC2: The bare verb writes no attestation: the shim passes sign=False through to review_plan; verified by test_shim_forwards_no_sign
AC3: `rebar review <id> --graph` and `rebar review <id> <reviewer_id>` each exit 2 with a message containing 'review-plan'; verified by test_graph_rejected and test_positional_reviewer_rejected
AC4: Three rows — cli:rebar review, lib:rebar.llm.review_ticket, mcp:review_ticket — exist in rebar._deprecations.REGISTRY, each with permanent=False and remove_in == 'v1.0.0'
AC5: rebar.llm.review_ticket still resolves and emits a DeprecationWarning when called, and the three internal call sites emit none; verified by test_public_warns_impl_is_silent
AC6: `rebar review --help` states the four differences (attestation, blocking, fast-fail, multi-pass); verified by test_help_states_the_behaviour_differences
AC7: `rebar review <closed-or-blocked-id>` exits 2 without an LLM call; verified by test_non_claimable_fast_fails
AC8: The fourteen existing direct callers of rebar.llm.review_ticket still pass unedited, proving the impl split is behaviour-preserving
AC9: A single MCP review_ticket invocation emits exactly one deprecation signal (the mcp log line); verified by test_mcp_tool_emits_one_signal
AC10: rebar clarity-check, rebar check-ac and rebar quality-check are untouched and still pass
AC11: default_reviewer_id() still resolves (ticket-quality entry keeps 'default': true) and select_reviewers / assemble_context remain in rebar.llm.operations.__all__
AC12: OUTPUT_SCHEMAS['review'] resolves to plan_review_verdict and review_result stays wired under the synthetic 'review_ticket' key; verified by test_schema_coverage
AC13: The four docs that describe the old contract are corrected — grep returns only deprecated lines, and docs/output-schemas.md line 57 reads plan_review_verdict for the review row
